title: He Built a Cabin by Hand in the Wilderness and Lived Alone for 30 Years

sections.name: Hook
lines: p_hook
In 1968, a man in his fifties flew deep into the Alaskan wilderness, with a few hand tools, and a plan.
p_title
His name was Dick Proenneke. And what he did next, people still talk about.

sections.name: Twin Lakes
lines: p_lake
He picked a spot on the shore of Twin Lakes, ringed by mountains, with no road in or out.
p_logs
The summer before, he had cut spruce logs, and left them to dry.

sections.name: Every log by hand
lines: p_axe
Now, with an axe, a saw, and tools he made himself, he notched each log, and stacked them one by one.
p_camera
He even filmed himself, with a camera on a tripod, so others could see how it was done.
p_cabin
Before winter came, the cabin was finished. Roof, door, windows, and a stone fireplace.

sections.name: Thirty winters
lines: p_winter
And then, he stayed. Through long, dark winters far below freezing.
p_journal
He fished, gardened, watched the wildlife, and wrote in his journal almost every day.
p_plane
A bush pilot flew in his supplies and mail. Otherwise, he was mostly alone, for about thirty years.

sections.name: What he left
lines: p_book
His journals became a book. His film became a much-loved documentary.
p_today
And his cabin still stands. Today, it's protected as part of a national park.
d_outro
Follow for more moments from history you won't forget.
